## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	// The work item — the queue's one durable object (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §3, §4).
2	// An issue titled `[claudinite-work] <pack>/<task> [qualifier]`, whose labels are
3	// its state, whose body's first line is the task path, and whose optional body
4	// fields (`Not-before`, `Blocked-by`, and a request's `Request` / `Model`) are the
5	// only facts it carries beyond that.
6	//
7	// PURE, and deliberately the whole schema: everything else — anchors, guards,
8	// yields, leashes, verdicts — is computed fresh at every scheduler run and pick from the
9	// engine and the declarations at HEAD (DESIGN §14). The label-and-field vocabulary
10	// here is therefore the compatibility surface across engine versions, which is why
11	// additive change is the strongly preferred shape and a rename needs a migration.
12	//
13	// Parse/serialize of those fields lives here and nowhere else (DESIGN §9).
14	//
15	// The one import, and a frozen constant at that: the pack-rename map, which this
16	// module needs to keep reading titles written before a rename (see parseWorkItemTitle).
17	import { canonicalPackId } from '../../../engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs';
18	
19	// The title prefix. Disjoint from the slot mechanism's `[claudinite-task]` on
20	// purpose: the two mechanisms coexist per-repo behind `taskScheduler.dispatch`,
21	// and neither may read the other's issues (DESIGN §14, S29).
22	export const WORK_PREFIX = '[claudinite-work]';
23	
24	// --- the canonical vocabulary (DESIGN §4, the migration of #1119) -------------
25	// Every label the machinery writes is one of three things — the item's single
26	// STATUS, its lifelong ORIGIN, or the URGENCY flag — and all of them live in the
27	// `task:` namespace. These are the spellings a reader compares against: decode
28	// first (`statusOf`, `originOf`), then compare, so an item filed by any engine
29	// version answers the same question the same way.
30	export const STATUS_PREFIX = 'task:status:';
31	export const PARK_PREFIX = `${STATUS_PREFIX}needs-human-`;
32	
33	export const STATUS_BLOCKED = `${STATUS_PREFIX}blocked`;
34	export const STATUS_READY = `${STATUS_PREFIX}waiting-for-executor`;
35	export const STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR = `${STATUS_PREFIX}running-executor`;
36	export const STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT = `${STATUS_PREFIX}running-agent`;
37	export const STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION = `${PARK_PREFIX}action`;
38	export const STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION = `${PARK_PREFIX}decision`;
39	export const STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL = `${PARK_PREFIX}approval`;
40	export const STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE = `${PARK_PREFIX}failure`;
41	export const STATUS_DONE = `${STATUS_PREFIX}done`;
42	export const STATUS_REJECTED = `${STATUS_PREFIX}rejected`;
43	
44	// The four statuses an OPEN item may wear before it parks or converges. An open
45	// item wearing no decodable status at all is off the state machine — a torn label
46	// swap's leavings, which the janitor repairs (DESIGN §6.2, §11).
47	export const LIVE_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
48	  STATUS_BLOCKED, STATUS_READY, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT,
49	]);
50	// The park kinds, in the order a decoder prefers them when an item somehow wears
51	// more than one: `failure` first, because it is the conservative lane — the one
52	// that holds the task's lane rather than letting a broken task keep filing work.
53	export const PARK_KINDS = Object.freeze(['failure', 'action', 'decision', 'approval']);
54	export const PARK_STATUSES = Object.freeze(PARK_KINDS.map((k) => `${PARK_PREFIX}${k}`));
55	export const STATUS_LABELS = Object.freeze([
56	  ...LIVE_STATUSES, ...PARK_STATUSES, STATUS_DONE, STATUS_REJECTED,
57	]);
58	
59	// THE ORIGIN (DESIGN §3, decision §15.29) — who asked for this item, worn for the
60	// item's whole life beside whatever status it holds. Read here; the writers arrive
61	// with the write-side flip.
62	export const ORIGIN_PREFIX = 'task:origin:';
63	export const ORIGIN_PLANNED = `${ORIGIN_PREFIX}planned`;
64	export const ORIGIN_AD_HOC = `${ORIGIN_PREFIX}ad-hoc`;
65	export const ORIGIN_GITHUB = `${ORIGIN_PREFIX}github`;
66	export const ORIGIN_LABELS = Object.freeze([ORIGIN_PLANNED, ORIGIN_AD_HOC, ORIGIN_GITHUB]);
67	
68	// --- the write spellings ------------------------------------------------------
69	// What this engine APPLIES — the canonical vocabulary above, since the write-side
70	// flip (#1119). The names survive the flip because fielded pack versions import
71	// them: a pack still on the old engine's spelling writes a legacy label, which
72	// every decoder here reads as the status it always meant.
73	export const BLOCKED = STATUS_BLOCKED;
74	export const READY = STATUS_READY;
75	export const URGENT = 'task:urgent';
76	export const EXECUTING = STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR;
77	export const AGENT = STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT;
78	export const TASK_DONE = STATUS_DONE;
79	export const TASK_OBSOLETE = STATUS_REJECTED;
80	
81	// --- the legacy spellings, written never and read forever ----------------------
82	// Every spelling any fielded engine has written. They are literals rather than
83	// aliases of the constants above precisely because those constants moved: a decode
84	// map built from them would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten
85	// the vocabulary it exists to read (DESIGN §4).
86	export const LEGACY_BLOCKED = 'task:blocked';
87	export const LEGACY_READY = 'task:ready';
88	export const LEGACY_EXECUTING = 'task:executing';
89	export const LEGACY_AGENT = 'task:agent';
90	
91	// @deprecated The bare park of the two-label era. A park is ONE label now
92	// (`task:status:needs-human-<kind>`); this is still read — on its own it decodes to
93	// `failure`, the conservative lane — and still ensured, because an open item filed
94	// by a fielded engine wears it.
95	export const NEEDS_HUMAN = 'needs-human';
96	
97	// @deprecated Nothing writes this since the approval park: a run that left an
98	// unmerged PR no longer CLOSES as delivered, it parks at the approval lane and
99	// waits to be merged. Kept exported, kept in `QUEUE_LABELS`, and still read
100	// everywhere it was read — closed issues carrying it are stored data, and a decoder
101	// that stopped recognising it would turn every historical delivered run into an
102	// un-outcomed one.
103	export const OUTCOME_DELIVERED = 'outcome:delivered';
104	
105	// @deprecated The pre-2026-08-19 terminal spellings. Kept exported so a fielded
106	// pack that imports them still loads, and READ wherever an outcome is decoded:
107	// labels are stored data on closed issues fleet-wide, so a decoder that stopped
108	// recognising these would turn every historical run into an un-outcomed one.
109	export const OUTCOME_DONE = 'outcome:done';
110	export const OUTCOME_OBSOLETE = 'outcome:obsolete';
111	
112	// @deprecated The pre-#1119 terminal spellings in the `task:` namespace, the
113	// generation between `outcome:*` and today's statuses. Read forever, same reason.
114	export const LEGACY_TASK_DONE = 'task:done';
115	export const LEGACY_TASK_OBSOLETE = 'task:obsolete';
116	
117	// @deprecated The origin marker (DESIGN §15.26). Nothing writes it and nothing
118	// branches on it: whether an item is a task's standing occurrence or an ad-hoc run
119	// is STRUCTURAL — see `isStandingItem` — so a marker that could disagree with the
120	// structure was a second authority over the same fact. Kept exported and inert
121	// because open items filed by an older engine still carry it, and a reader that
122	// choked on an unknown label would fail on exactly those.
123	export const ORIGIN_SCHEDULE = 'origin:schedule';
124	
125	// THE PARK KINDS. A park is ONE label since the flip — `task:status:needs-human-<kind>`
126	// — and the kind is what the human is being asked for, which is the whole
127	// difference between a queue a person can skim and one they have to read.
128	//
129	// The four are disjoint by REMEDY, not by cause:
130	//   action   — something outside the code must change: a secret set, a scope
131	//              granted, a routine's prompt or endpoint fixed, an item re-created
132	//              with the parameter it was missing. Mechanical; no judgement.
133	//   decision — the run stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice:
134	//              re-queue or abandon, does the half-done work stand, was the
135	//              ceiling violation acceptable.
136	//   approval — the run SUCCEEDED and deliberately left an unmerged PR. The only
137	//              park that is not a fault; the human merges it or closes it.
138	//   failure  — the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or
139	//              forged item. Someone diagnoses and fixes code.
140	// `failure` is the default a park falls back to, so an unclassified park reads as
141	// "diagnose me" rather than quietly joining the mechanical lane.
142	//
143	// The names are the ones fielded packs import; their VALUES are today's park
144	// statuses. The two-label era's sub-labels (`task:needs-human-<kind>`) are read by
145	// `parkOf` below and written by nobody.
146	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION = STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_ACTION;
147	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION = STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION;
148	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL = STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL;
149	export const NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE = STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE;
150	export const TRIAGE_LABELS = PARK_STATUSES;
151	
152	// WHICH PARKS HOLD THE TASK'S LANE. A task's open STANDING item is the occurrence
153	// itself, so while one exists the generator files no further occurrence
154	// (`planSchedulerRun` job 1) — which for a park means the task stops being scheduled at
155	// all until a human clears it. That is right for a `failure`: filing a queue of
156	// items that will break the same way helps nobody, and the silence is the signal.
157	// It is wrong for the other three, which are a person's inbox, not a fault in the
158	// task: a PR waiting to be approved, a choice waiting to be made and a secret
159	// waiting to be set must not also stop tomorrow's run.
160	//
161	// A park wearing NO sub-label blocks, which is what makes this safe on the way in:
162	// every item parked by an engine older than the sub-labels, and every kind word a
163	// future engine invents that this one does not know, holds the lane rather than
164	// silently letting a broken task keep filing work.
165	export const isBlockingPark = (item) => statusOf(item) === STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE;
166	
167	// --- the decode (DESIGN §4, "legacy spellings — written never, read forever") --
168	// Labels are STORED DATA: open items filed by a fielded engine wear its spellings,
169	// closed items keep theirs forever, and members converge on their own schedules. So
170	// every reader here goes through one pass that maps every spelling ever written
171	// straight to today's — never through a literal comparison against one of them.
172	const LEGACY_STATUS = new Map([
173	  [LEGACY_BLOCKED, STATUS_BLOCKED],
174	  [LEGACY_READY, STATUS_READY],
175	  [LEGACY_EXECUTING, STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR],
176	  [LEGACY_AGENT, STATUS_RUNNING_AGENT],
177	  [LEGACY_TASK_DONE, STATUS_DONE], [OUTCOME_DONE, STATUS_DONE],
178	  [LEGACY_TASK_OBSOLETE, STATUS_REJECTED], [OUTCOME_OBSOLETE, STATUS_REJECTED],
179	]);
180	
181	const LEGACY_PARK_RE = /^task:needs-human-(.+)$/;
182	
183	// The park an issue's labels name, canonical, or null. Both shapes decode here:
184	// today's single `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` and the legacy pair
185	// (`needs-human` plus a sub-label). A kind nobody here knows — a bare legacy park,
186	// or a word a newer engine invented — reads as `failure`, the conservative lane.
187	function parkOf(names) {
188	  const kinds = [
189	    ...names.filter((n) => n.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX)).map((n) => n.slice(PARK_PREFIX.length)),
190	    ...names.map((n) => LEGACY_PARK_RE.exec(n)?.[1]).filter(Boolean),
191	  ];
192	  if (!kinds.length && !names.includes(NEEDS_HUMAN)) return null;
193	  return `${PARK_PREFIX}${PARK_KINDS.find((k) => kinds.includes(k)) ?? 'failure'}`;
194	}
195	
196	// Every distinct status an issue's labels decode to. One entry per status, so an
197	// item mid-flip — wearing a legacy spelling beside its canonical one — reads as the
198	// ONE status it is, and only genuinely conflicting labels read as more than one
199	// (the dashboard's `torn`).
200	export function statusesOn(issue) {
201	  const names = labelNames(issue);
202	  const out = new Set();
203	  const park = parkOf(names);
204	  if (park) out.add(park);
205	  for (const n of names) {
206	    if (STATUS_LABELS.includes(n) && !n.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX)) out.add(n);
207	    else if (LEGACY_STATUS.has(n)) out.add(LEGACY_STATUS.get(n));
208	  }
209	  return [...out];
210	}
211	
212	// THE status an issue wears, canonical, or null for one wearing none. A park wins
213	// over anything else present: a torn transition that left a state label beside a
214	// park must read as parked, or the queue would pick up an item a human owns.
215	export function statusOf(issue) {
216	  const worn = statusesOn(issue);
217	  return worn.find((s) => s.startsWith(PARK_PREFIX))
218	    ?? STATUS_LABELS.find((s) => worn.includes(s))
219	    ?? null;
220	}
221	
222	export const isStatus = (issue, status) => statusOf(issue) === status;
223	export const isParked = (issue) => (statusOf(issue) ?? '').startsWith(PARK_PREFIX);
224	export const parkKindOf = (issue) =>
225	  (isParked(issue) ? statusOf(issue).slice(PARK_PREFIX.length) : null);
226	
227	// The origin an issue wears, or null. Unlike the status there is no legacy
228	// spelling to fold in: `origin:schedule` is inert stored data (see ORIGIN_SCHEDULE),
229	// and reading it as an origin would put a marker nothing writes back into play.
230	export const originOf = (issue) =>
231	  labelNames(issue).find((n) => ORIGIN_LABELS.includes(n)) ?? null;
232	
233	// Every spelling that MEANS `status` — what a transition out of it has to clear,
234	// since the item may wear any engine's. Leaving a park clears every park spelling
235	// whatever its kind: a re-queue takes the item out of the human's hands entirely.
236	export function spellingsOf(status) {
237	  if (String(status ?? '').startsWith(PARK_PREFIX)) {
238	    return [...PARK_STATUSES, ...PARK_KINDS.map((k) => `task:needs-human-${k}`), NEEDS_HUMAN];
239	  }
240	  const legacy = [...LEGACY_STATUS].filter(([, canonical]) => canonical === status).map(([l]) => l);
241	  return [status, ...legacy];
242	}
243	
244	// THE RE-QUEUE LEVER, in words — one home, because it is written into every message
245	// that parks an item and a stale copy of it is an instruction that no longer works.
246	// Clearing the status IS the re-ask (DESIGN §16.3): a park is one label now, so
247	// there is nothing else to take off.
248	export const requeueHint = `clear its status label and add \`${STATUS_READY}\``;
249	
250	// A kind word (from a worker's own triage marker, or a call site) to the park it
251	// names. Anything unrecognised is a `failure`: a worker that misspells its class has
252	// a bug, which is exactly what that lane means.
253	export const triageLabelFor = (kind) =>
254	  (PARK_KINDS.includes(kind) ? `${PARK_PREFIX}${kind}` : STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE);
255	
256	
257	// The stored-data rename rule, decode side: every spelling ever written maps
258	// STRAIGHT to the canonical word, in one pass — including `outcome:delivered`,
259	// which nothing writes any more but closed issues carry forever.
260	const OUTCOME_WORDS = new Map([[STATUS_DONE, 'done'], [STATUS_REJECTED, 'obsolete']]);
261	
262	// The one outcome an issue's labels carry, as the canonical word ('done',
263	// 'delivered', 'obsolete') or null. Everything that tallies or renders outcomes
264	// decodes through here, so a spelling change is one map entry and not a sweep.
265	export function outcomeOf(issue) {
266	  // `statusesOn` rather than `statusOf`: a closed item's terminal write is its
267	  // outcome even when a park label stands beside it, and park precedence is a
268	  // question about LIVE items — what the queue may pick up — not about history.
269	  const worn = statusesOn(issue);
270	  for (const [status, word] of OUTCOME_WORDS) if (worn.includes(status)) return word;
271	  return hasLabel(issue, OUTCOME_DELIVERED) ? 'delivered' : null;
272	}
273	
274	// --- the request vocabulary, retired (DESIGN §4's legacy table, §16.1) --------
275	// @deprecated The three labels the SHADOW-ITEM request model used. The mark is
276	// `task:origin:ad-hoc` now and the marked issue is the item itself, so nothing here
277	// applies these — but they are read forever: `claude-task` is still accepted as a
278	// mark (a person with it in muscle memory, a template that carries it), and an
279	// issue whose shadow item is still draining wears `claude-queued`.
280	//
281	// What survives the retirement is the reason the mark is a LABEL at all: it must be
282	// appliable from the issue page on a phone, and it is write-gated by the platform —
283	// applying a label needs triage or write access — which is the first half of the
284	// security story (the second is the precondition's permission read at pickup,
285	// §16.4). A request's PARAMETERS are body fields (`parseRequestFields`), gated on
286	// the author's push access instead, and no label carries one: a `claude-model:` or
287	// `claude-automerge` label applied by hand asks for nothing.
288	export const REQUEST_LABEL = 'claude-task';
289	export const QUEUED_LABEL = 'claude-queued';
290	export const IN_REVIEW_LABEL = 'claude-in-review';
291	
292	// The families a request may ask for in its `Model:` field. `none` is not among
293	// them: a request is implemented by a session, so an agentless family would name a
294	// run that cannot happen.
295	export const REQUEST_MODELS = Object.freeze(['opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku']);
296	
297	// The four state labels an open item may wear. An open item wearing none of them
298	// and no `needs-human` is off the state machine entirely — a torn label swap's
299	// leavings, which the janitor repairs (DESIGN §6.2, §11).
300	export const STATE_LABELS = [BLOCKED, READY, EXECUTING, AGENT];
301	
302	// The canonical statuses the same four decode to — what a reader tests against,
303	// since an item may wear either engine's spelling (`statusesOn`).
304	export { LIVE_STATUSES as STATE_STATUSES };
305	
306	// Every label this mechanism applies, with the colour and description a bootstrap
307	// one-off would have given it. Ensured create-if-missing before anything is
308	// applied: GitHub 422s when you apply an unknown label and never creates one on
309	// demand, so the thing that assigns a label guarantees it first.
310	//
311	// The LEGACY block below is ensured too, and that is deliberate: nothing writes
312	// those spellings any more, but open items filed by a fielded engine wear them and
313	// deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it — including closed
314	// ones, which are stored data (DESIGN §4).
315	export const QUEUE_LABELS = [
316	  { name: STATUS_BLOCKED, color: 'c5def5', description: 'Claudinite queue: waiting on Blocked-by and/or Not-before' },
317	  { name: STATUS_READY, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite queue: available for an executor to pick up' },
318	  { name: URGENT, color: 'd93f0b', description: 'Claudinite queue: pick this before any non-urgent item' },
319	  { name: STATUS_RUNNING_EXECUTOR, color: 'fbca04', description: 'Claudinite queue: an executor holds the claim' },

334	  { name: LEGACY_AGENT, color: '1d76db', description: 'Claudinite queue (legacy): an agent session owns this item' },
335	  { name: NEEDS_HUMAN, color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue (legacy): parked for a human' },
336	  { name: LEGACY_TASK_DONE, color: '0e8a16', description: 'Claudinite queue (legacy): succeeded, nothing pending' },
337	  { name: LEGACY_TASK_OBSOLETE, color: 'ededed', description: 'Claudinite queue (legacy): never ran' },

340	
341	// GitHub hands labels back as objects on the issues API and as bare strings in
342	// some fixtures; accept either.
343	export const labelNames = (issue) =>
344	  (issue?.labels ?? []).map((l) => (typeof l === 'string' ? l : l?.name)).filter(Boolean);
345	
346	export const hasLabel = (issue, name) => labelNames(issue).includes(name);
347	
348	// Title. The optional qualifier exists ONLY for deliberately concurrent items —
349	// a fan-out naming its target — and it is part of the identity the same-title
350	// mutex reads (DESIGN §6.1). Nothing ever encodes a date here: that was the slot
351	// grammar, and the issue number is the identity (DESIGN §5).
352	export const workItemTitle = ({ pack, task, qualifier = null }) =>
353	  `${WORK_PREFIX} ${pack}/${task}${qualifier ? ` ${qualifier}` : ''}`;
354	
355	// pack and task ids are single path segments; the qualifier is whatever follows.
356	const TITLE_RE = /^\[claudinite-work\]\s+([^/\s]+)\/([^/\s]+)(?:\s+(\S.*))?$/;
357	
358	// The pack half is canonicalized on the way out. A work item's title is STORED
359	// DATA — it sits on an open GitHub issue that outlives any one converge — so items
360	// filed before a pack was renamed still carry the old spelling. Read literally, the
361	// scheduler run would not recognise its own live item, would file a second one beside it, and
362	// would leave the first orphaned in the queue with nothing ever draining it.
363	export function parseWorkItemTitle(title) {
364	  const m = TITLE_RE.exec(String(title ?? '').trim());
365	  return m ? { pack: canonicalPackId(m[1]), task: m[2], qualifier: m[3]?.trim() || null } : null;
366	}
367	
368	export const isWorkItemTitle = (title) => parseWorkItemTitle(title) !== null;
369	
370	// The `<pack>/<task>` id a WORKER PATH names — the identity half a marked issue's
371	// title cannot carry (DESIGN §16.1), read off the path its machine block names. Two
372	// shapes, because tasks have two homes: the `tasks/` slot a declared pack contributes,
373	// and the queue's own built-in root. The `.claudinite/shared/` prefix is optional in
374	// both — a member's mount is there and the canon runs its own tree.
375	//
376	// THE BUILT-IN ROOT HAS TWO SPELLINGS, and both are permanent. The surface moved from
377	// `engine/scheduler/` to the tasks pack (#1317), so a live item minted before the move
378	// still names the engine path while every new one names the pack path; the wire id
379	// either produces is unchanged, which is what the move promised. Stored data is
380	// renamed on the DECODE side or it stops decoding, and here that failure is silent:
381	// this is the fallback for a marked issue, whose title is the requester's own words,
382	// so a path that yields null leaves the item unattributable rather than rejected.
383	//
384	// It is a PARSE, not a lookup: anything that must know the task exists at HEAD
385	// resolves the path against the discovered task set instead (the executor does).
386	const PACK_TASK_PATH_RE = /^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?packs\/([^/]+)\/tasks\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+$/;
387	const BUILT_IN_TASK_PATH_RE = /^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?(?:engine\/scheduler|packs\/claudinite-tasks)\/queue\/tasks\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+$/;
388	
389	export function taskIdFromPath(path) {
390	  const p = String(path ?? '');
391	  const pack = PACK_TASK_PATH_RE.exec(p);
392	  if (pack) return { pack: canonicalPackId(pack[1]), task: pack[2] };
393	  const builtIn = BUILT_IN_TASK_PATH_RE.exec(p);
394	  return builtIn ? { pack: 'engine', task: builtIn[1] } : null;
395	}
396	
397	// STANDING OR AD-HOC, DERIVED (DESIGN §15.26). A task's standing item is the one
398	// the generator files at an anchor: its title names the task and nothing else, and
399	// the task it names is on a calendar. Everything else is ad-hoc — a `manual` task
400	// (which has no anchor to stand for) and every qualified item (a fan-out target, a
401	// request naming its issue), each of which may legitimately run beside the
402	// occurrence rather than being it.
403	//
404	// It is read off the item and the declaration at HEAD rather than off a label the
405	// creator applied, because the two could disagree: a marker says what its writer
406	// believed, the structure says what the item IS, and the guards that consume this
407	// (the occurrence guard, the dedupe, the `after` yield) are only sound on the
408	// second. `frequency` is the declared frequency of the task the title names —
409	// absent when the repo no longer carries it, which is ad-hoc by the same rule.
410	export function isStandingItem(item, frequency) {
411	  const parsed = parseWorkItemTitle(item?.title ?? item);
412	  return !!parsed && parsed.qualifier === null && frequency != null && frequency !== 'manual';
413	}
414	
415	// --- comment markers ----------------------------------------------------------
416	// The three comments the protocol reads back. They are HTML comments so a human
417	// reading the item sees prose, and they are here — with the labels and the body
418	// fields — because together they ARE the item's vocabulary, the one compatibility
419	// surface across engine versions (DESIGN §14).
420	//
421	// The CLAIM comment carries who and when (executor identity is an unbounded set
422	// and must never become a label). The HANDOFF comment names the session and the
423	// invocation nonce. The EPISODE comment is the boundary the claim arbiter is
424	// scoped to: every claim before it is dead, and arbitrating over dead claims makes
425	// one outrank every future live claimant — the item then livelocks through reclaim
426	// cycles forever (F18). A reclaim, a revert and a hand re-queue each write one.
427	export const CLAIM_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-claim -->';
428	export const HANDOFF_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-handoff -->';
429	export const EPISODE_MARKER = '<!-- claudinite-episode -->';
430	
431	// --- the body -----------------------------------------------------------------
432	
433	export const NOT_BEFORE_FIELD = 'Not-before';
434	export const BLOCKED_BY_FIELD = 'Blocked-by';
435	
436	// The three fields a REQUEST item carries (DESIGN §16.3, §16.11). `Request` is the issue this
437	// run implements — the whole payload, since the request task has no code-work phase
438	// to hand one over. `Model` is the family the asker chose, copied here by the scheduler run
439	// from a write-gated label and read only by a task that declares
440	// `model_from_request`; it is the first thing an item carries that defines
441	// behaviour, which is why it is fenced rather than waved through (§16.7).
442	export const REQUEST_FIELD = 'Request';
443	export const MODEL_FIELD = 'Model';
444	
445	// `Task` is the TARGETING field (DESIGN §16, the one-issue request): which task a
446	// marked issue asks for, as `<pack>/<task>`. Absent, the ask is the built-in
447	// request implementer, which is what an ordinary "implement this issue" mark means.
448	// It rides the same author gate as `Model` and `Merge`: naming a task is choosing
449	// what runs, and a body is editable by whoever opened the issue.
450	export const TASK_FIELD = 'Task';
451	
452	// `Merge` is the asker's standing authorization, copied here from the
453	// write-gated `claude-automerge` label. Its one value is `if-narrow`: the run may
454	// land its own pull request when the diff classifier calls the diff narrow, and
455	// must park for approval otherwise. An absent field is the default — never merge —
456	// so an item an older scheduler run wrote reads as unauthorized rather than as authorized.
457	export const MERGE_FIELD = 'Merge';
458	export const MERGE_IF_NARROW = 'if-narrow';
459	
460	// The heading the delivered-artifacts section carries in a work item body. One
461	// home, because it is written in three places and MATCHED when a re-entrant run
462	// updates the section it already wrote.
463	export const DELIVERED_HEADING = 'Delivered by code-work';
464	
465	// The same heading as earlier renames spelled it. A live item's body still carries
466	// whichever word was current when its section was first written, and matching only
467	// today's would append a SECOND section rather than updating that one.
468	export const LEGACY_DELIVERED_HEADINGS = Object.freeze([
469	  'Delivered by prework',
470	  'Delivered by code_work',
471	]);
472	
473	// --- the machine block (DESIGN §16.1, §16.3) ----------------------------------
474	// A one-issue request's item IS the issue somebody marked, so the item's fields
475	// share a body a person authored and keeps editing. They live in one delimited
476	// block, appended at adoption and rewritten in place after that: everything outside
477	// it belongs to the human, everything inside it to the machine, and a parser that
478	// read the whole body would take a sentence of prose for a field.
479	//
480	// A `[claudinite-work]` item has no block — its whole body is the machine's — so
481	// every reader here falls back to the whole text, which is what keeps items filed
482	// before the one-issue model draining unchanged.
483	export const MACHINE_BLOCK_START = '<!-- claudinite-item -->';
484	export const MACHINE_BLOCK_END = '<!-- /claudinite-item -->';
485	
486	const BLOCK_RE = /<!-- claudinite-item -->\n?([\s\S]*?)\n?<!-- \/claudinite-item -->/;
487	
488	// The machine's half of a body, or null where there is no block at all.
489	export const machineBlockOf = (body) => BLOCK_RE.exec(String(body ?? ''))?.[1] ?? null;
490	
491	// The machine's half to read fields out of: the block where there is one, the whole
492	// body otherwise.
493	export const itemFieldText = (body) => machineBlockOf(body) ?? String(body ?? '');
494	
495	// Replace the block, or append one to a body that has none. The human's text is
496	// never rewritten — an append lands after it, separated by a blank line.
497	export function withMachineBlock(body, block) {
498	  const text = String(body ?? '');
499	  const wrapped = `${MACHINE_BLOCK_START}\n${block.replace(/\s*$/, '')}\n${MACHINE_BLOCK_END}`;
500	  if (BLOCK_RE.test(text)) return text.replace(BLOCK_RE, wrapped);
501	  return `${text.replace(/\s*$/, '')}\n\n${wrapped}\n`;
502	}
503	
504	// Apply an edit to whichever half is the machine's. Every writer that reshapes an
505	// item body — a Context section, code-work's delivered list, a stamped
506	// `Not-before` — goes through here, so it edits the block on a marked issue and the
507	// whole body on a `[claudinite-work]` item, with one call site either way.
508	export function editItemBody(body, edit) {
509	  const block = machineBlockOf(body);
510	  return block === null ? edit(String(body ?? '')) : withMachineBlock(body, edit(block));
511	}
512	
513	// The human's half of a body — everything the machine block is not. A marked
514	// issue's PARAMETERS are read from here and never from the block: re-asking clears
515	// the status and leaves the previous run's block standing, and a parser that read
516	// the whole body would find that stale copy beside the person's own field.
517	export const humanTextOf = (body) => String(body ?? '').replace(BLOCK_RE, '').trim();
518	
519	const NOT_BEFORE_RE = /^Not-before:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
520	const BLOCKED_BY_RE = /^Blocked-by:[ \t]*(.*)$/m;
521	const REQUEST_RE = /^Request:[ \t]*#?(\d+)/m;
522	const MODEL_RE = /^Model:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
523	const MERGE_RE = /^Merge:[ \t]*(\S+)/m;
524	
525	// Build a work item body. The first line is the task path — the only thing an
526	// executor reads to locate the worker, validated in code before anything trusts
527	// it. Everything behavior-defining (model, ceiling, worker content, code-work
528	// command) is read from the tracked task files at HEAD, never from here.
529	export function workItemBody({
530	  taskPath, notBefore = null, blockedBy = [], context = [], delivered = [], reason = null,
531	  request = null, model = null, merge = null,
532	}) {
533	  const lines = [taskPath, ''];
534	  const fields = [];
535	  if (notBefore) fields.push(`${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${notBefore}`);
536	  if (blockedBy.length) fields.push(`${BLOCKED_BY_FIELD}: ${blockedBy.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')}`);
537	  if (request) fields.push(`${REQUEST_FIELD}: #${request}`);
538	  if (model) fields.push(`${MODEL_FIELD}: ${model}`);
539	  if (merge) fields.push(`${MERGE_FIELD}: ${merge}`);
540	  if (fields.length) lines.push(...fields, '');
541	  lines.push('Execute the Claudinite task above.');
542	  if (context.length) {
543	    lines.push(
544	      'The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it.',
545	      '',
546	      '### Context',
547	      ...context.map((c) => `- ${c}`),
548	    );
549	  }
550	  if (reason) lines.push('', '### Why the agent is here', '', `- ${reason}`);
551	  if (delivered.length) lines.push('', `### ${DELIVERED_HEADING}`, '', ...delivered.map((d) => `- ${d}`));
552	  return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
553	}
554	
555	// The `Blocked-by` numbers a body names, from a work item's body or from an
556	// ORDINARY issue's — a request marked for implementation states what it waits on in
557	// the same field spelling, and adoption carries it onto the item it births (§16.11).
558	export function parseBlockedBy(body) {
559	  const bb = BLOCKED_BY_RE.exec(String(body ?? ''))?.[1] ?? '';
560	  return [...bb.matchAll(/#(\d+)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]));
561	}
562	
563	// Parse an item body back into the facts the scheduler run and the executor read. A body
564	// with no first line, or whose fields are absent, yields nulls — absence is
565	// meaningful everywhere here and is never filled in with a default.
566	export function parseWorkItemBody(body) {
567	  const text = itemFieldText(body);
568	  const taskPath = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).find((l) => l !== '') ?? null;
569	  const nb = NOT_BEFORE_RE.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim() || null;
570	  const blockedBy = parseBlockedBy(text);
571	  const request = REQUEST_RE.exec(text) ? Number(REQUEST_RE.exec(text)[1]) : null;
572	  // An unrecognised family reads as absent rather than as itself: the item's model
573	  // is behaviour-defining, so the only values that leave this parser are ones the
574	  // engine can actually dispatch at (§16.7).
575	  const askedModel = MODEL_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
576	  const model = REQUEST_MODELS.includes(askedModel) ? askedModel : null;
577	  // Same fencing as the model: an unrecognised authorization reads as absent, and
578	  // absent is the safe end of this field — a run that cannot read its permission
579	  // opens a pull request and waits.
580	  const askedMerge = MERGE_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
581	  const merge = askedMerge === MERGE_IF_NARROW ? askedMerge : null;
582	  return { taskPath, notBefore: nb, blockedBy, request, model, merge };
583	}
584	
585	// WHAT A MARKED ISSUE ASKS FOR (DESIGN §16.3, §16.7, §16.11) — read from the
586	// person's own text at every adoption, so each ask names its parameters afresh and
587	// nothing stale outranks a new one.
588	//
589	// `gated` is whether the issue's AUTHOR holds push access. A body is editable by
590	// whoever opened the issue where a label was write-gated by the platform, so the
591	// three behaviour-defining fields are honoured only for an author who could have
592	// applied them as labels anyway; an ungated ask still runs, at the default task and
593	// model and with no authorization to land anything.
594	export function parseRequestFields(body, { gated = false } = {}) {
595	  const text = humanTextOf(body);
596	  const asked = {
597	    task: /^Task:[ \t]*(\S+)/m.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null,
598	    model: MODEL_RE.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null,
599	    automerge: /^Automerge:[ \t]*(\S+)/m.exec(text)?.[1]?.toLowerCase() ?? null,
600	  };
601	  const blockedBy = parseBlockedBy(text);
602	  const notBefore = NOT_BEFORE_RE.exec(text)?.[1]?.trim() || null;
603	  if (!gated) return { task: null, model: null, merge: null, blockedBy, notBefore, ungated: Object.values(asked).some(Boolean) };
604	  return {
605	    task: /^[^/\s]+\/[^/\s]+$/.test(asked.task ?? '') ? asked.task : null,
606	    // An unrecognised family reads as absent rather than failing the request: a run
607	    // nobody can start would look accepted forever.
608	    model: REQUEST_MODELS.includes(asked.model) ? asked.model : null,
609	    merge: ['if-narrow', 'yes', 'true'].includes(asked.automerge) ? MERGE_IF_NARROW : null,
610	    blockedBy,
611	    notBefore,
612	    ungated: false,
613	  };
614	}
615	
616	// The item's own `### Context` bullets, in order — the binding scope a hand-created
617	// item was born with. Read back rather than kept only for the agent to read,
618	// because an operator's PARAMETERS ride here: `create-work-item --context
619	// "REPOS=Alpha Beta"` is how a forced run says what it is running on, and the
620	// executor hands these lines to code-work as `CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT`.
621	//
622	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body — the same
623	// bounds `withSection` writes to — and only `- ` bullets count, so the prose
624	// framing around a section contributes nothing.
625	function sectionLines(body, heading) {
626	  const lines = String(body ?? '').split('\n');
627	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() === `### ${heading}`);
628	  if (at === -1) return [];
629	  const out = [];
630	  for (const line of lines.slice(at + 1)) {
631	    if (line.startsWith('### ')) break;
632	    const m = /^-[ \t]+(.*)$/.exec(line);
633	    if (m) out.push(m[1].trim());
634	  }
635	  return out;
636	}
637	
638	export const parseContextLines = (body) => sectionLines(body, 'Context');
639	
640	// --- the roll's record ----------------------------------------------------------
641	
642	// The section a no-go roll keeps on the item: the last declined reason and the next
643	// wake, REPLACED on every roll (the item is a status line, not a log — the timeline
644	// carries the history). Serializer and parser live together so the shape has one
645	// home; the executor writes it, and anything answering "why didn't it run" — the
646	// dashboard above all — reads it back.
647	export const LAST_VERDICT_HEADING = 'Last verdict';
648	
649	export function lastVerdictLines({ at, reason, until }) {
650	  const lines = [`${at} — the precondition declined: ${reason}`];
651	  if (until) lines.push(`Asked again at ${until}.`);
652	  return lines;
653	}
654	
655	export function parseLastVerdict(body) {
656	  const lines = sectionLines(body, LAST_VERDICT_HEADING);
657	  // The reason may carry the separator itself, so the split is on the FIRST match.
658	  const first = /^(.*?) — the precondition declined: ([\s\S]*)$/.exec(lines[0] ?? '');
659	  if (!first) return null;
660	  const until = lines.map((l) => /^Asked again at (.*?)\.?$/.exec(l)).find(Boolean)?.[1] ?? null;
661	  return { at: first[1], reason: first[2], until };
662	}
663	
664	// Fold a second set of Context lines into the first, keeping order and dropping
665	// exact duplicates. Both sides are real scope — the item carries what its creator
666	// bound it to, the precondition adds what this occurrence found — and a set-write
667	// from either side would drop the other's.
668	export const mergeContext = (...groups) => [...new Set(groups.flat().filter((l) => l && l.trim()))];
669	
670	// Stamp (or clear) `Not-before` on an existing body, in place where the field is
671	// already present and directly under the task path otherwise. Text surgery rather
672	// than a rebuild: the body also carries the creating precondition's Context and
673	// code-work's Delivered section, which belong to whoever wrote them.
674	export function withNotBefore(body, iso) {
675	  const text = String(body ?? '');
676	  if (NOT_BEFORE_RE.test(text)) {
677	    return iso
678	      ? text.replace(NOT_BEFORE_RE, `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`)
679	      : text.replace(/^Not-before:[ \t]*.*\n?/m, '');
680	  }
681	  if (!iso) return text;
682	  const lines = text.split('\n');
683	  const at = lines.findIndex((l) => l.trim() !== '');
684	  if (at === -1) return `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}\n`;
685	  lines.splice(at + 1, 0, '', `${NOT_BEFORE_FIELD}: ${iso}`);
686	  return lines.join('\n');
687	}
688	
689	// Set a section of an item body (the Context, code-work's Delivered, the agent's Why)
690	// — replacing one of the same heading if it is already there, appending otherwise.
691	//
692	// REPLACING IS THE WHOLE POINT, and appending was a live bug (#879). Every standing
693	// item is born carrying a `### Context`, and the hand-off writes Context again — so
694	// an append leaves TWO sections of that name, while the session is told to read "the
695	// issue's Context section", singular. The one it reads first is then the scheduler run's birth
696	// note and the binding scope is in the other, which fails silently whichever section
697	// the agent picks. It also grows: an item re-queued through hand-off twice carried a
698	// third.
699	//
700	// A section runs to the next `### ` heading or to the end of the body, so a replaced
701	// section keeps its position rather than migrating to the bottom — the body stays in
702	// the order a reader learned it.
703	// `aliases` are older spellings of the SAME heading. The section is rewritten under
704	// `heading`, but located by any of them, so a body written before a rename is updated
705	// in place instead of gaining a second section.
706	export function withSection(body, heading, lines, aliases = []) {
707	  if (!lines.length) return body;
708	  const text = String(body ?? '').replace(/\s*$/, '');
709	  const section = [`### ${heading}`, '', ...lines.map((l) => `- ${l}`)];
710	  const existing = text.split('\n');
711	  const wanted = new Set([heading, ...aliases].map((h) => `### ${h}`));
712	  const at = existing.findIndex((l) => wanted.has(l.trim()));
713	  if (at === -1) return `${text}\n\n${section.join('\n')}\n`;
714	  const after = existing.findIndex((l, i) => i > at && l.startsWith('### '));
715	  const tail = after === -1 ? [] : ['', ...existing.slice(after)];
716	  return `${[...existing.slice(0, at), ...section, ...tail].join('\n')}\n`;
717	}

13	skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
14	ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is

# tidy-issues worker

The **acting** half of the repo tidy-up: triage the issues in scope, then record what you did. The run's
**Context section is binding scope** — it lists the issues to triage. Work only those; don't enumerate the
repo yourself. GitHub access is **MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

This task writes **issues only** (its triage actions and its own tracker). It never opens, closes, merges,
or comments on a PR — that dimension belongs to `tidy-prs`, which is assess-only.

## 1. Triage each issue

For each issue in the Context list, run the [single-issue-triage](../../skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)
skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is
inconclusive it **comments, doesn't close** — and an issue whose verdict is the one the skill
already posted there returns `unchanged`, written to nowhere. Collect what each triage did.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

**Only a run that changed something reaches the tracker.** What counts is a triage action actually taken —
an issue closed, a comment posted — or something this run leaves for a human. `left` and
`unchanged` are not actions. A run that worked its whole Context list and took no action has
**nothing to record**: leave the tracker exactly as found, no body rewrite and no comment, and
create none if it doesn't exist. The scan itself is not news.

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** when there is something to record and it
is absent — creation always lands an issue open and ignores a `state: closed` argument, so create it and
close it in a second call (never a fresh issue per run, never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension
keeps its **own** tracker, so the two tasks never race to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways on a run that has something to record:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the actions taken this run and anything left
  for a human. The body is the live picture — it replaces yesterday's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)

Repos tidied before the split carry a single combined tracker titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Repo
Tidy`. If it exists and its body doesn't already say so, rewrite the body to one line pointing at the
per-dimension trackers (`Tidy Issues`, `Tidy PRs`) and stop there — nothing else to do on it, and never
open, close, or reopen it. Already pointing at them ⇒ skip. Absent ⇒ skip; never create it.

5	// Worker: task.md. PRs are a separate task: one dimension per task, each with its
6	// own trigger, scope, and tracker — no ordering barrier between them.
7	//
8	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
9	
10	export default {
11	  id: 'tidy-issues',
12	  frequency: 'daily',                       // the 04:00 anchor (DESIGN §2) — the one tidy dimension that ACTS, so latency matters
13	  precondition_signals: ['issues', 'commits'],
14	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                    // "implemented in main" is a judgment call against main's current content
15	  expected_outcome: 'none',                 // writes ISSUES only (the triage actions + its own tracker) — never a PR
16	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
17	  agent_execution_timeout: 900,             // one dimension over a bounded issue list
18	
19	  // ONE trigger, and one widener. The trigger is a touched issue: if no issue was
20	  // filed, commented on, labelled, or reopened in the window, this task does not
21	  // run — the existing pile got the same triage last time it moved, and re-deriving
22	  // it costs an agent run per day to rewrite the tracker with itself.
23	  //
24	  // The task's own triage comments are the one write that lands on the issues this
25	  // gate watches, so re-announcing a standing verdict would arm tomorrow's run
26	  // forever (#988). single-issue-triage does not make that write; nothing here
27	  // filters it out after the fact.
28	  //
29	  // A substantive default-branch move WIDENS an already-triggered run to every open
30	  // issue, because a real commit can implement an issue the issue itself never
31	  // recorded — but it no longer wakes the task by itself. On any repo whose `main`
32	  // moves most days that widening was firing daily, which is a full re-triage of
33	  // every open issue every day: exactly the "went over the existing ones with
34	  // nothing new" this gate exists to prevent. A housekeeping-only move (a nightly
35	  // baseline commit, a bot bump) implements nothing, so it does not widen at all.
36	  precondition(signals) {
37	    const substantive = signals.commits?.substantiveChange === true;
38	
39	    // A `task:*` label is the scheduler's own marker, stamped on a queue work item
40	    // when it is created and carried for its whole life. The issues signal hides
41	    // those items by TITLE prefix, so one the queue files under any other title
42	    // reaches this task and gets triaged as project work. The label is the
43	    // invariant, so it is what this filters on — and it filters BOTH ways: such an
44	    // issue is neither a touch that triggers a run nor a target inside one.
45	    const queueItem = (i) => (i.labels ?? []).some((l) => String(l).startsWith('task:'));
46	    const open = (signals.issues?.open ?? []).filter((i) => !queueItem(i)).map((i) => i.number);
47	    const inScope = new Set(open);
48	    const touched = (signals.issues?.touched ?? []).filter((n) => inScope.has(n));
49	
50	    // Between the signal's title filter and the label filter above, none of
51	    // Claudinite's own issues — the queue's work items, its schedule board, the
52	    // standing trackers — can be triaged as project work or count as the touch
53	    // that triggers a run.
54	    if (!touched.length) return { run: false, reason: 'no issues touched in the window' };
55	
56	    const scope = substantive ? open : touched;
57	    return {
58	      run: true,
59	      reason: substantive
60	        ? `issues touched, and main moved substantively — re-check all ${scope.length} open issue(s) against it`
61	        : 'issues touched in the window',
62	      context: [`Issues to triage: ${scope.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')}.`],
63	    };
64	  },

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

1	// The machine-readable records a task's execution leaves in an Actions log
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2), and the parsers that read them back.
3	//
4	// TWO FAMILIES, ONE OF THEM HISTORICAL. `claudinite-task-run` was the SLOT
5	// scheduler's own line, one per due task per run; the slot scheduler is retired
6	// (#974) and nothing writes that line any more. The parser stays, and only the
7	// parser: Actions logs from before the retirement are still inside their retention
8	// window, and the usage fold still counts them. Nothing new should be taught this
9	// shape — `claudinite-task-exec` below is the live record.
10	//
11	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
12	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside.
13	
14	// The five things a slot scheduler run could do with a due task. One name per
15	// outcome, used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no
16	// mapping table between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
17	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
18	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an agent session ran this task.
19	  'agent',
20	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (code-work is the
21	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose code-work requested no agent phase.
22	  // Kebab, not the declaration field's `code_work`: this word is a WIRE token,
23	  // constrained to the line format's `[a-z-]+` charset.
24	  'code-work',
25	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
26	  'skipped',
27	  // Its code-work failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
28	  'failed',
29	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
30	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
31	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
32	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
33	  'deferred',
34	]);
35	
36	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
37	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
38	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
39	
40	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
41	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
42	// half-parsing it.
43	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
44	const VERSION = 'v1';
45	
46	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
47	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
48	// printed nothing at all.
49	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
50	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
51	);
52	
53	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
54	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
55	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
56	// The code phase has been renamed twice, and job logs outlive both renames:
57	// `preprocess` (pre-2026-08-06) and `prework` (pre-2026-08-18) are the earlier
58	// words for what is now `code-work`. Runs logged under either still parse, each
59	// normalized straight to the canonical word.
60	// Exported because the outcome words are also the usage aggregate's counter KEYS,
61	// and that file holds rows written under the older words. Its decode renames them
62	// by this same map, so a rename never silently drops a historical count.
63	export const LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze({ preprocess: 'code-work', prework: 'code-work' });
64	
65	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
66	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
67	  if (!m) return null;
68	  const [, pack, task, slotId, word] = m;
69	  const outcome = LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES[word] ?? word;
70	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
71	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
72	}
73	
74	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
75	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
76	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
77	  const out = [];
78	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
79	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
80	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
81	  }
82	  return out;
83	}
84	
85	// --- executor-side execution records ------------------------------------------
86	// The historical records above say what the retired slot scheduler DID with a due
87	// task; these record what an EXECUTOR SESSION did with the work it ran. Printed by executor-side code
88	// (resolve-dispatch on a terminal verdict, record-exec.mjs at convergence), they
89	// land in the session transcript, ride to the conversation-logs branch with the
90	// executor's capture step, and the usage fold counts them deterministically —
91	// the "task statuses out of the conversation logs" half of the census (owner,
92	// 2026-08-06). Same single-home rule: renderer and parser sit here together.
93	
94	export const TASK_EXEC_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
95	  // The dispatch ran to completion within its ceiling; the issue was closed.
96	  'success',
97	  // The run failed (task failure or ceiling violation); converged to needs-human.
98	  'failed',
99	  // The dispatch named a task the repo no longer carries (file gone, pack
100	  // undeclared) — the executor closed the issue as obsolete. Not a failure.
101	  'task-gone',
102	  // The dispatch was malformed (bad path shape, unparseable declaration) and was
103	  // converged to needs-human without running.
104	  'invalid',
105	]);
106	
107	export const TASK_EXEC_TAG = 'claudinite-task-exec';
108	
109	// The bracketed field is the OCCURRENCE'S IDENTITY, which is a different thing under
110	// each dispatch mechanism: a slot id (`d2026-08-06`) where slots decide what runs, and
111	// the work item's issue number (`#867`) where the queue does. `slotId` keeps its name
112	// for the fielded records that already carry one; what it must never become is a
113	// constant, since it is the only join from a record back to the work it describes.
114	export const renderTaskExec = ({ pack, task, slotId, status }) =>
115	  `${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} ${pack}/${task} [${slotId ?? 'unknown'}] ${status}`;
116	
117	const EXEC_LINE_RE = new RegExp(
118	  String.raw`(?:^|\s)${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
119	);
120	
121	export function parseTaskExec(line) {
122	  const m = EXEC_LINE_RE.exec(line);
123	  if (!m) return null;
124	  const [, pack, task, slotId, status] = m;
125	  if (!TASK_EXEC_STATUSES.includes(status)) return null;
126	  return { pack, task, slotId, status };
127	}
128	
129	export function parseTaskExecs(text) {
130	  const out = [];
131	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
132	    const rec = parseTaskExec(line);
133	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
134	  }
135	  return out;
136	}
